chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nuflī, from al-Sakkūnī, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled regarding a man who made the divorce of his wife in the hands of two men; one of them divorced her, but the other refused. The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) rejected validating that until they both agree together on the divorce.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on divorce if two agents are given authority but only one executes it?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), citing Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (AS), establishes the principle of joint agency in divorce, requiring consensus between two delegated agents for the act to be valid. It highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on precision in conditional delegations, ensuring that the authority is exercised collectively rather than unilaterally by one party. This ruling underscores the importance of mutual agreement in legal transactions within the family law framework.
